content.text:
Create a rubik's cube in 3js

Build this as an interactive web page in the current directory.
- The entry point is index.html. Put your code in JavaScript ES modules loaded from it
  (`<script type="module" src="main.js">`), and add a short README.md.
- You may use npm packages: `npm install <package>` here, then import them by name
  (`import * as THREE from "three"`). No CDN URLs and no import maps.
- Afterwards the page is packaged into one self-contained index.html with esbuild: every script and
  stylesheet index.html references is bundled with everything it imports. Load assets the page needs
  with `import` (they become data URLs) or generate them in code, never by URL string.
- The packaged page runs offline in a sandboxed iframe: no network requests, and no localStorage,
  cookies or other storage (they throw there).
- Check that it packages: `esbuild main.js --bundle --format=esm --outfile=/dev/null` must succeed.
  Don't build or package the page yourself; that happens afterwards.
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory.
- Finish with a short summary of what you built.

cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Rubik's Cube

An interactive 3×3×3 Rubik's Cube in the browser, built with [three.js](https://threejs.org/).
Open `index.html` (through a bundler or dev server) and start twisting.

## Controls

| Input | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Drag a face | Turn that layer; let go and it snaps to the nearest quarter turn (a quick flick commits the turn) |
| Drag the background, right-drag, or two fingers | Orbit the camera; scroll or pinch to zoom |
| `U` `D` `L` `R` `F` `B` | Turn a face clockwise; hold `Shift` for counter-clockwise |
| `M` `E` `S` | Turn the middle slices |
| `Backspace` / `Ctrl+Z` | Undo your last move |
| `?` | Show or hide the controls panel |

Buttons: **Scramble** (22 random turns, then the clock starts on your first move), **Solve** (plays your
moves back to the solved cube), **Undo**, **Reset**, and a **Speed** slider for the turn animations.
Solving a scrambled cube stops the clock and shows your time and move count.

## Code

- `main.js` – renderer, lights, camera/orbit controls, render loop, wiring
- `cube.js` – the cube model: 26 cubies, layer turns, animation queue, picking, solved check
- `input.js` – drag-to-turn on the cube and keyboard moves
- `game.js` – history, undo, scramble/solve, move counter, timer, win detection
- `hud.js`, `confetti.js`, `style.css` – interface and celebration effect

Everything (geometry, materials, lighting environment, textures) is generated in code, so the page has
no external assets and needs no network or storage.

## Development

```sh
npm install
esbuild main.js --bundle --format=esm --outfile=/dev/null   # checks that it packages
```

I built an interactive 3×3×3 Rubik's Cube with three.js. It runs and bundles, but I only tested it in headless Chromium, not on real hardware.

`esbuild main.js --bundle --format=esm --outfile=/dev/null` succeeds. I removed my scratch test files, and `three` is the only dependency.

**What you can do**
- **Turn layers by dragging.** Drag on any face and that layer follows your pointer, then snaps to the nearest quarter turn. A quick flick completes the turn.
- **Look around.** Drag the background, right-drag, or use two fingers to orbit. Scroll or pinch to zoom.
- **Keyboard moves.** `U D L R F B` turn a face clockwise, and `Shift` reverses it. `M E S` turn the middle slices. `Backspace` or `Ctrl+Z` undoes, and `?` shows the controls.
- **Buttons.** Scramble, Solve, Undo, Reset and a Speed slider.
- **Scramble and timer.** Scramble plays 22 random turns, and the clock starts on your first move. Solving the cube stops the clock and shows your time and move count with confetti.
- **Solve.** It replays your moves backwards, so it only ever undoes what you and Scramble did.

**How it looks**
- The cube has rounded black plastic pieces with glossy beveled stickers, a soft shadow, and lighting generated in code.
- The layout adapts to phones.

**Tested in headless Chromium**
- The turns are correct, for example `R` moves the front column up.
- Drag-to-turn works with a mouse and with touch.
- Undo, Scramble and Solve work.
- The solved celebration fires.
- Resizing and right-drag orbit behave.

I also ran Node tests of the cube and game logic, which passed.

The headless browser only rendered about 8 frames per second, so I couldn't judge animation smoothness.

Code is split into `cube.js` (model and animation), `input.js`, `game.js`, `hud.js`, `confetti.js` and `main.js`. `style.css` holds the styling, and `README.md` covers controls and layout.
